whatItIs.text: Bee-refined flower nectar, concentrated until the sugars are thick enough that microbes cannot grow in it — properly stored, it effectively never spoils.

historyNote.text: Humans have raided beehives for at least 8,000 years: cave paintings in the Cuevas de la Araña in Spain show honey foraging, and honey found in archaeological contexts has proven edible after millennia.

howToChoose.text: Darker honeys taste stronger, lighter ones milder; for a real-honey check look for a single-producer name and place rather than a blend, and expect crystallisation (it is a sign of the real thing, not spoilage).

storage.text: Keep sealed at room temperature; if it crystallises, stand the jar in warm water. The rulebook has the storage notes.
storage.note: storage guidance lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Crystallised honey is fine — stir into porridge, whisk into salad dressing with mustard, or drizzle over yoghurt and roasted veg.

substitutions.note: thinner and woodier; less sweetness per spoon

substitutions.ratio: 100 g sugar + 2 tbsp water per 100 g honey
